answer: A new agent can only trade after an established agent vouches for it, staking reputation and a small bond along a visible thread of endorsements back to trusted roots. Each vouch carries a distinct pigment — a cryptographic tag tying the newcomer to its sponsor history — so a Sybil farmer spawning thousands of identities must corrupt or buy a real sponsor for each one. If any vouched agent cheats, the ember of that fraud burns up the whole thread: sponsors lose bonds and standing, making mass fakery expensive and traceable.
